paras: The shooting of a fleeing prisoner in Maysville, Kentucky, took place on the night of September 19, 1882, when special policeman Fred. Bodie shot a Black man who had broken away from him after an arrest for obstructing the sidewalk. The man, whose name was not printed, was wounded in the hip, an injury the local paper described as slight.

According to the Maysville Evening Bulletin, Bodie arrested the man, whom it called "a negro," for obstructing the sidewalk and took him to the station house. Before he could be confined, the man "broke from the officer and ran." The paper said he was ordered to stop several times and, "not obeying the command," was shot by the officer, who "inflicted a slight wound in the negro's hip."
The coverage does not report the man's name, his medical condition after the shooting, any charge against him, or any inquiry into the officer's use of his weapon.

The only known report is a single unheadlined paragraph on the third page of the Evening Bulletin of September 20, 1882, printed among notices for the county fair, a ball, and store advertisements. The item gave only the officer's side, stressing that the man had been ordered to stop several times and calling the wound slight. No other paper's account of the shooting appears in the coverage.
